status: PROPOSED ONLY — requires independent exact-field review

fields.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
fields.before: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
fields.after: If any fault should come to light, you would still not escape execution.
fields.rationale: Restores second-person warning; no beheading is specified.

fields.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
fields.before: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'
fields.after: Better to delay and postpone the appointed time. Empress Jia will surely harm the crown prince; then depose her and avenge him. That alone will be enough to count as a merit, and only then can you achieve your aim.'
fields.rationale: Restores postponement and the condition for achieving the aim.

fields.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
fields.before: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
fields.after: Better to delay and postpone the appointed time. Empress Jia will surely harm the crown prince; then depose her and avenge him. That alone will be enough to count as a merit, and only then can you achieve your aim."
fields.rationale: Restores postponement and the condition for achieving the aim.

fields.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
fields.before: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
fields.after: Xiu then used counter-agents to spread word that people inside the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome back the crown prince.
fields.rationale: Restores counter-agents and the plot to depose Jia.

fields.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
fields.before: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
fields.after: When the empress heard this she was alarmed and afraid, and ordered Cheng Ju, the court physician-in-chief, to compound pills of croton and apricot kernels.
fields.rationale: Names the office and ingredients, avoiding an unsupported poison label.

fields.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
fields.before: Lü jailed and starved Yu; sympathizers smuggled food over walls.
fields.after: Lü told Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince into a small compound and gave him no food at all; nevertheless, people in the palace passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
fields.rationale: Corrects the actor and restores the palace source of food.

fields.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
fields.before: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
fields.after: Lü then pressed the medicine on the crown prince, who refused to take it. When the crown prince went to the privy, Lü struck him dead with a medicine pestle. The crown prince cried out loudly, and his voice was heard outside.
fields.rationale: Restores attempted forced medicine, refusal, timing, and audible cry.

fields.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
fields.before: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
fields.after: This wish was not fulfilled, adding to my bitter regret.
fields.rationale: Preserves first-person memorial language.

fields.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
fields.before: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
fields.after: Although Yu's guilt could scarcely be greater, he is still a descendant of the sovereign. To send him to burial as an ordinary commoner truly moves me to pity. I especially beg Your Majesty's grace to grant him the rites of a prince.
fields.rationale: Preserves the argument without narrowing descendant to grandson.

fields.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
fields.before: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
fields.after: Although Yu's guilt could scarcely be greater, he is still a descendant of the sovereign. To send him to burial as an ordinary commoner truly moves me to pity. I especially beg Your Majesty's grace to grant him the rites of a prince.
fields.rationale: Preserves the argument and memorial voice.

fields.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
fields.before: I followed the testament and across set you up as heir to brighten our ancestors.
fields.after: In obedience to his final command, I established you as heir apparent, to bring glory to our ancestors.
fields.rationale: Renders the succession command intelligibly and preserves first person.

fields.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
fields.before: Hui claimed he installed Yu by Wu Di's will.
fields.after: In obedience to his final command, I established you as heir apparent, to bring glory to our ancestors.
fields.rationale: Restores quotation and the glory to the ancestors.

fields.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
fields.before: Hui likened the plot to classic wronged heirs.
fields.after: But I was blind to the vicious plotting, so that you suffered the calamity of an unnatural death: Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji have appeared again in our own day.
fields.rationale: Restores first-person responsibility and the named comparisons.

fields.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
fields.before: He credited ministers for Jia's fall.
fields.after: Thanks to the wisdom of my ministers, and to the indignation of people and spirits, my mind was opened. I punished those responsible, and all received the penalty for their crimes.
fields.rationale: Restores people and spirits, awakening, and punishment.

fields.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
fields.before: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?
fields.after: But how can this lessen the cruel suffering of your unjustly afflicted spirit?
fields.rationale: Restores the rhetorical question about the wronged spirit.

fields.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
fields.before: Ritual could not unkill Yu.
fields.after: But how can this lessen the cruel suffering of your unjustly afflicted spirit?
fields.rationale: Restores the rhetorical question rather than commentary.

fields.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
fields.before: Imperial rhetoric of inner ache.
fields.after: Thus grief and regret shake me to my innermost being.
fields.rationale: Translates the quoted grief in the first person.

fields.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
fields.before: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.
fields.after: When the funeral procession set out, a great wind arose with thunder and lightning, and its curtains and canopies were blown apart.
fields.rationale: Restores lightning and both kinds of covering.

fields.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
fields.before: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
fields.after: When the funeral procession set out, a great wind arose with thunder and lightning, and its curtains and canopies were blown apart.
fields.rationale: Restores lightning and avoids narrowing canopies to umbrellas.

fields.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
fields.before: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.
fields.after: From childhood you were endowed with outstanding gifts; your fragrant virtue grew luxuriant.
fields.rationale: Restores the childhood qualities and image.

fields.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
fields.before: Praise for childhood brilliance.
fields.after: From childhood you were endowed with outstanding gifts; your fragrant virtue grew luxuriant.
fields.rationale: Translates the line rather than summarizing it.

fields.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
fields.before: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
fields.after: Already in early childhood you showed lofty intelligence and exceptional distinction.
fields.rationale: Avoids reducing childhood to tied hair.

fields.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
fields.before: Boyhood distinction.
fields.after: Already in early childhood you showed lofty intelligence and exceptional distinction.
fields.rationale: Restores childhood and the specific qualities.

fields.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
fields.before: Wu Di's praise.
fields.after: Long ago your sage ancestor prized your goodness and fine qualities.
fields.rationale: Retains the expressed ancestor without naming an individual in this line.

fields.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
fields.before: Therefore we installed you heir to light imperial foundations forever.
fields.after: Therefore you were established as heir, to continue the imperial foundation forever.
fields.rationale: Corrects the sense of continuing rule.

fields.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
fields.before: Heir establishment recalled.
fields.after: Therefore you were established as heir, to continue the imperial foundation forever.
fields.rationale: Translates the poetic line.

fields.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
fields.before: Rhetorical grief at murder.
fields.after: How could the cruel and violent secretly plot, bringing calamity like this?
fields.rationale: Preserves plotting without adding a murder allegation.

fields.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
fields.before: Seasonal mourning tropes.
fields.after: Sorrow moves the harmonious breath of nature; anguish reaches through the four seasons.
fields.rationale: Restores both source images.

fields.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
fields.before: Funeral lament pause.
fields.after: Alas, how sorrowful!
fields.rationale: Translates the lament.

fields.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
fields.before: Hui blamed himself.
fields.after: That you were degraded and deposed was truly due to my blindness.
fields.rationale: Restores first person and the addressee’s deposition.

fields.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
fields.before: Yu died east at Xu.
fields.after: Now you too bear a grievance in the east.
fields.rationale: Does not assert a death location absent from this line.

fields.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
fields.before: Universal mourning asserted.
fields.after: Among all those who possess understanding, who is not stricken with grief?
fields.rationale: Restores the rhetorical question.

fields.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
fields.before: Justice spans dynasties.
fields.after: Though the ages differ, the pattern is the same; past and present follow one principle.
fields.rationale: Restores the source parallelism.

fields.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
fields.before: Tomb closure comforts ghost.
fields.after: The burial chamber has now been prepared, and your spirit will be laid to rest.
fields.rationale: Restores the prepared tomb and rest of the spirit.

fields.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
fields.before: Mourning cortège splendor.
fields.after: A vast array of feathered canopies; rank upon rank of officials.
fields.rationale: Restores the images and ordered officials.

fields.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
fields.before: Courtiers weep together.
fields.after: All share the same grief and pain: who does not feel bitter sorrow?
fields.rationale: Does not restrict shared grief to courtiers.

fields.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
fields.before: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
fields.after: He was given the posthumous name Minhuai.
fields.rationale: Uses posthumous naming instead of canonization.

fields.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
fields.before: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
fields.after: On the jimao day of the sixth month, he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.
fields.rationale: Restores the cyclical day without a Western date.

fields.zh: 臧字敬文。
fields.before: Second son Zang, styled Jingwen.
fields.after: Zang's courtesy name was Jingwen.
fields.rationale: Removes unsupported birth order.

fields.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。
fields.before: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.
fields.after: In the fourth month of Yongkang's first year, he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.
fields.rationale: Restores year one.

fields.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。
fields.before: Zang named grand-heir.
fields.after: Now I establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.
fields.rationale: Restores the voice of the edict.

fields.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
fields.before: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.
fields.after: The crown prince's officials shall immediately become officials of the imperial grandson-heir.
fields.rationale: Restores change of the crown-prince officials.

fields.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
fields.before: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.
fields.after: The crown prince's officials shall immediately become officials of the imperial grandson-heir.
fields.rationale: Restores change of the crown-prince officials.

fields.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
fields.before: Prince Zhao of Lun acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir.'
fields.after: Lun, Prince of Zhao, shall act as Grand Mentor to the imperial grandson-heir.'
fields.rationale: Corrects the reversed name and principality.

fields.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
fields.before: Prince Zhao of Lun acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir."
fields.after: Lun, Prince of Zhao, shall act as Grand Mentor to the imperial grandson-heir."
fields.rationale: Corrects the reversed name and principality.

fields.zh: 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也。
fields.before: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.
fields.after: In the fifth month, Lun and the imperial grandson went together to the Eastern Palace. The grandson went out through the Western Side Gate; his carriage, dress, and attendants were all those formerly used by Minhuai.
fields.rationale: Restores Lun, the joint journey, and attendants.

fields.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。
fields.before: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.
fields.after: When they reached Bronze Camel Street, the palace attendants wept, the attendants all sobbed, and passersby wiped away their tears.
fields.rationale: Restores the named groups without assuming gender.

fields.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
fields.before: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.
fields.after: The mulberry tree grew again in the western wing; when the imperial grandson was deposed, it withered.
fields.rationale: Corrects the location to the western wing.

fields.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
fields.before: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.
fields.after: The mulberry tree grew again in the western wing; when the imperial grandson was deposed, it withered.
fields.rationale: Translates the source rather than interpreting the omen.

fields.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
fields.before: In the first month of Yongning year one Prince Zhao of Lun usurped the throne, degrading him to Prince of Puyang—together with the emperor he moved to Jinyong and soon after was murdered.
fields.after: In the first month of Yongning's first year, Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne. He reduced the grandson to Prince of Puyang; the grandson and the emperor were both moved to Jinyong, and the grandson was killed soon afterward.
fields.rationale: Corrects the reversed title and preserves the joint transfer.

fields.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
fields.before: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.
fields.after: In the first month of Yongning's first year, Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne. He reduced the grandson to Prince of Puyang; the grandson and the emperor were both moved to Jinyong, and the grandson was killed soon afterward.
fields.rationale: Restores the ruler, emperor’s transfer and avoids asserting the location of death.

fields.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。
fields.before: Tai'an era canonized Ai.
fields.after: Early in Tai'an he was posthumously given the name Ai.
fields.rationale: Uses posthumous naming instead of canonization.

fields.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
fields.before: Editors praise Yu's childhood gifts.
fields.after: The historian says: Minhuai showed a remarkably intelligent bearing and a precociously mature nature.
fields.rationale: Restores the historian’s explicit voice and the quoted content.

fields.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
fields.before: The realm expected greatness.
fields.after: All under Heaven turned their hearts toward him and had considerable hopes for his future.
fields.rationale: Restores turning of hearts and future hope.

fields.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
fields.before: Hui's blindness and court cowardice blamed.
fields.after: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover what was hidden, and none of the many officials showed the integrity of a remonstrating minister.
fields.rationale: Restores discernment and remonstrance.

fields.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
fields.before: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!
fields.after: Although the rites of mourning and honor were complete and the grief and pity profound, how could they help the one who had suffered such cruelty?
fields.rationale: Avoids claiming literal poisoning or innocence.

fields.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
fields.before: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
fields.after: Although the rites of mourning and honor were complete and the grief and pity profound, how could they help the one who had suffered such cruelty?
fields.rationale: Translates the rhetorical question without inventing poisoning.

fields.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
fields.before: Verse praises innate wit.
fields.after: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
fields.rationale: Translates the encomium in its stated voice.

fields.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
fields.before: Court awaited his reign.
fields.after: His imperial grandfather treasured him; the assembled officials craned their necks in expectation.
fields.rationale: Restores grandfather and posture without inventing an anticipated reign.

fields.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
fields.before: Death ended every hope of restoration.
fields.after: Once he fell victim to ruthless cruelty, hope for his return was in vain.
fields.rationale: Does not restrict the line’s cruelty to death.

fields.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
fields.before: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
fields.after: At the time observers of portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven, so he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, with a fief of fifty thousand households.
fields.rationale: Does not over-specify observers as astrologers.

fields.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
fields.before: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
fields.after: The court made an extensive selection of men of virtue and standing as his tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
fields.rationale: Restores the criterion of virtue and standing while preserving all offices.

fields.zh: 永康元年四月，封為襄陽王。
fields.before: In Yongkang fourth month he was made Prince of Xiangyang.
fields.after: In the fourth month of Yongkang's first year, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiangyang.
fields.rationale: Restores year one.

fields.zh: 永寧元年八月，立為皇太孫。
fields.before: In Yongning eighth month he was made imperial grandson-heir.
fields.after: In the eighth month of Yongning's first year, he was established as imperial grandson-heir.
fields.rationale: Restores year one.
